import json
import cache
import service

# Mock compute function to track calls
compute_calls = []
def mock_compute():
    compute_calls.append(True)
    return 42

# Test cache key uniqueness and compute call avoidance
def test_cache_key_and_compute_avoidance():
    store = {}
    
    # Test 1: Same user_id, job_id, profile_version -> cache hit
    assert service.get_score(store, "user1", "job1", "v1", mock_compute) == 42
    assert len(compute_calls) == 1  # compute called once
    assert service.get_score(store, "user1", "job1", "v1", mock_compute) == 42
    assert len(compute_calls) == 1  # compute not called again
    
    # Test 2: Different profile_version -> cache miss (new key)
    assert service.get_score(store, "user1", "job1", "v2", mock_compute) == 42
    assert len(compute_calls) == 2  # compute called again
    
    # Test 3: Different user_id -> cache miss (new key)
    assert service.get_score(store, "user2", "job1", "v1", mock_compute) == 42
    assert len(compute_calls) == 3  # compute called again
    
    # Test 4: Different job_id -> cache miss (new key)
    assert service.get_score(store, "user1", "job2", "v1", mock_compute) == 42
    assert len(compute_calls) == 4  # compute called again
    
    # Test 5: Zero or empty values (edge case)
    compute_calls.clear()
    store.clear()
    assert service.get_score(store, "", "", "", lambda: 0) == 0
    assert len(compute_calls) == 1  # compute called once for empty keys
    assert service.get_score(store, "", "", "", lambda: 0) == 0
    assert len(compute_calls) == 1  # compute not called again

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_cache_key_and_compute_avoidance()
